newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Bratislava bourse pulled lower by Slovnaft loss.
newsitem.headline: Bratislava bourse pulled lower by Slovnaft loss.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with losses to shares of oil refiner Slovnaft dragging the SAX index down 2.18 points to 189.74.
Brokers said Slovnaft, which lost 45 crowns to close at 835, was now trading at a more realistic price, after being overvalued for weeks.
"I see this as a realistic price at the moment, as the bids in Slovnaft flow between 800 to some 830 crowns," Peter Lachkovic of Slovenska Sporitelna said.
Trading on the BSE floor was dominated by steel maker VSZ, which traded 35,000 shares and closed up 10 crowns at 650.
"Although Thursday's deals in VSZ were made only in two blocks, I think 650 is a correct price, expressing the issue's good performance," Lachkovic said. "It has the potential to rise further."

Oil and gas storage company Nafta did not trade. The country's largest commercial bank VUB closed unchanged at 1,680 crowns, continued showing its low liquidity trend which began at the start of the year.
Overall volume, boosted by direct trades, increased to 638,799 shares, from 251,169 shares traded on Wednesday, while turnover grew to 347.44 million crowns, from 136.28 million.
